summary: Redesign the desktop sidebar around what each chat needs from the user (option C of the sidebar mock). Recents rows become two lines: a status dot, the title and the time, then a full-width muted status line. Recents is grouped into Needs you (an open approval, question or plan, or an error), Working and Done recently, with Needs you and Working always shown in full above Show N more. Needs you comes from the backend's own record of open cards (provider:get-pending-requests plus the live request/question/plan events), not from the transcript. The This Mac workspace tree folds behind one summary row and offline remote machines behind one Remote machines row, both persisted through the settings table, and the workspace count reads "14 projects" with the thread count in a tooltip.

reactNativeIos.followUpRelease: mobile-v0.5.0. The phone's ConversationsScreen already renders the two-line row this change brings to desktop (status dot and title on line 1, the turnPreviewLine preview on line 2), so only the Needs you group is missing. It is not small: the list is per project and knows a thread's state only once that thread has been opened in the chat store, so grouping by pending cards needs a per-row pending-request fetch (or a batched channel) and a SectionList. It ships in mobile-v0.5.0 behind the local mobile_conversations_needs_you flag, reusing applyPendingRequestEvent from src/shared/pending-requests.ts for the live updates.

nativeAndroid.followUpRelease: Android 0.6.0. BrowseScreen's conversation list has the same gap as the React Native one: pending cards are recovered only for the open thread (the pending-request-recovery work), so a Needs you group needs per-row pending state from the backend first. It ships with Android 0.6.0 behind the android_conversations_needs_you preference, with the same open, close, error or stop, and next-user-message rules as the shared reducer, ported to Kotlin and checked against the same cases.

storageDataMigration.reason: No schema change and no migration. The two disclosures are new rows in the existing key-value settings table, sidebar.localTreeExpanded and sidebar.offlineMachinesExpanded, read by hydrateSidebarCollapse in layout-store.ts; an absent key means collapsed, so an older database needs no backfill and an older client never reads them. This Mac used to be expanded unless its id was in sidebar.collapsed.machines; that key still drives each remote machine's own disclosure, and a stale 'local' entry in it is now ignored, so an existing user sees This Mac folded once after upgrading and one click restores it for good. Pending cards are held in memory only, as before.

updateRelease.reason: Renderer and shared-contract change only. No package identity, signing, deep link, update channel or wire-protocol change: the sidebar reads the existing provider:get-pending-requests channel (capability pending_requests_v1) and the existing runtime events.
